The standard warranty lasts 36 months or 30,000 km, whichever comes first, from the date of sale to the first owner. The warranty carries over to each later owner for the balance of the remaining warranty period. A second or later owner should tell the nearest Royal Enfield Service Centre about the purchase and fill in the form it asks for to use the warranty. The emission-control warranty also applies after a change of ownership, provided its conditions are met from the date of original sale. Parts of the evaporative emission control system have a different period, 24 months from the date of first use, so confirm the period with an authorised Royal Enfield service centre. The warranty applies only if all maintenance and services are done within the warranty period and the kilometre ranges in the schedule, at a Royal Enfield Authorised Dealer or Service Centre.

rows.text: Park the motorcycle upright on a level surface. Start the engine from cold, let it idle for 2 to 3 minutes, then stop it. Wait 2 to 3 minutes for the oil to settle, then read the sight glass. The oil level should be close to the MAX mark. If it is not, top up the oil to MAX and repeat the procedure. Do not fill the oil above the MAX mark, as overfilling may affect clutch function.

Make sure the motorcycle is upright and on its centre stand. Make sure the gears are in neutral and the neutral lamp is glowing in the instrument console. Switch OFF both the ignition and the stop switch, wait a few seconds, then switch the ignition and the stop switch ON again to start the engine. Watch out: Pull in and hold the clutch lever before using the electric start. Watch out: Push and hold the electric start switch until the engine starts, for a maximum of 5 seconds. Watch out: If the malfunction indicator does not turn OFF, get the motorcycle checked through a Royal Enfield Authorised Service Centre.

rows.text: Long press the Mode button on the right-hand switch cube to change the instrument cluster from analog to digital. Spray the chain with the recommended chain cleaning solvent while you turn the rear wheel. Make sure the whole chain is covered with the solvent, and use a suitable brush on hard deposits if needed. Wait a few minutes, then clean the chain thoroughly to remove dirt and grime. Turn the rear wheel slowly and apply the recommended chain lubricant to the chain links. After a few minutes, wipe off the excess lubricant with a clean cloth. The manual schedules cleaning, lubricating and adjusting the chain every 500 km (or earlier as required), or after riding in wet, dusty or muddy conditions. The manual does not name a specific chain cleaner or chain lubricant; it refers to the recommended ones.

To top up the expansion tank, remove its cap and fill the tank to the upper level line. Then replace the expansion tank cap. For coolant, the manual names Coolant from Total, which is ready to use and does not need mixing. Check the coolant level in the expansion tank every 1000 km (or earlier as required) and top up as required. Watch out: Do not open a radiator cap when the engine is hot. The pressure can make the coolant boil and spurt out, causing severe burns. Watch out: Do not spill coolant. Avoid skin or body contact with it, and wash any affected area promptly with soap and water. The manual names only Coolant from Total. It does not give a coolant specification for other brands. The manual does not say whether the engine must be cold before the expansion tank cap is removed.

rows.text: Place the motorcycle upright on a firm, level surface. Check that the brake fluid reservoir is horizontal. Front brake: the fluid level should be at the center of the window, which the manual treats as the minimum level. Rear brake: the fluid level should be between the MAX and Min marks. Clean the filler cap before removing it, and use only DOT 4 brake fluid from a sealed container. Refill with the same type of brake fluid, which is DOT 4. Use only the brake fluid the manual specifies, because other fluids can cause the rubber seals to deteriorate and leak. Keep water and dust out of the brake fluid reservoir when refilling. Watch out: Brake fluid is highly corrosive and can damage painted parts. Clean any spill immediately with a soft cloth, preferably wet. Watch out: Do not let brake fluid touch your skin, eyes or clothing. Watch out: An insufficient brake fluid level will cause the brake system to fail. Watch out: Do not mix DOT 4 with other brake fluid.
